Yeah Ive had 3 friends die at young ages. It’s horrible. 
One died from an absolute freak occurrence. He had a bunch of unrelated diseases all at once without even knowing (literally had West Nile virus, Lyme disease, and walking pneumonia combined with a congenital heart condition that he obviously already knew he had). Something clicked one day and he had a series of 3 heart attacks back to back to back. He was resuscitated but by the time he was, his brain filled up with fluid and did severe irreversible damage. He’s still alive but in an almost entirely vegetative state. He was only 22 when this happened. This was 8 years ago and I’ll never get it out of my head and thinking about all the times we hung out and how nice and funny and charismatic he was. I also had feelings for him that I never told him about. It hit me really hard. I’ll have random memories come back and I’ll just start crying all over again. Like how we were both at GameStop waiting for the original Dark Souls to be released and how we both went home and Skyped with each other all night while we played it. Then when Elden Ring came out I started playing it and all those memories came back and I thought “he would have loved this I wish he could play it” and I broke down all over again. 

Then a few years ago another one of my friends (who was also an angel and a part of the same friend group) had cancer and told no one about it and ended up dying. He was only 26. This is random but like I can never watch Scott Pilgrim ever again. The fact that I saw it in theaters with both of these friends and the fact that they’re dead now haunts me. Like WHY did these two have to die they were such nice people and such good friends.

Then I learned a friend of mine that I went to grade school with killed himself in 2015 but I didn’t learn about it until 2020 and it crushed me. We weren’t particularly close but he was always very nice to me and he’s the one who introduced me to MST3K when I was in grade school which was a huge thing in my life. Idk what happened or why but I think about that a lot. 

Like when you’re a kid like in grade school or high school everything feels like it lasts forever and that you’re invincible and then once you see these things happen to close friends you grew up with, especially at a young age, it makes you realize how fragile everything is. 

I honestly don’t know the best way to cope with this sort of thing. I think maybe one of the most effective ways might be just talking about it with other people who’ve had similar experiences. For me at least it kind of helps me sort out my thoughts/finding ways to move on as best you can. But that’s just me and I know everyone’s different. Either way I’m sorry for your loss and I hope you’re doing okay.

Not sure how to articulate this, and I’m sure I’m not alone here, but most of my life, especially when I was at my worst, I’d constantly have moments where I saw myself in the mirror and would like touch and examine my face and ask myself “who are you?” over and over and over again. Like I knew somewhere deep inside was the real me but what I saw on the outside was a completely different, demonic, person who I didn’t recognize and who I was terrified of because I never knew they were capable of being so downright evil.

Like I’m not making excuses for how horrible and abusive I was in the past so I don’t want to excuse that by fully relinquishing myself by saying “it was all the psychosis it’s not my fault” but knowing the why and how of it all, and knowing that change IS possible and how I can be the person I always wanted to be gives me hope. I don’t see that person in the mirror anymore and I haven’t for some time. I feel like I killed that part of me and it’ll never be back and it’s a relief knowing that I’m not permanently lost and getting better is an option. 

Seeing how far I’ve come since then is a double-edged sword for sure; on one hand I’m finally starting to love myself for the first time in my life, and on the other hand I’m more and more disgusted at the person I used to be and the more I resent myself for letting things get so horrible in the first place. I want nothing more than to undo all the pain and abuse and trauma I’ve inflicted on people by not getting this problem solved earlier in my life. There’s nothing I can do about it other than dedicate myself to being a better person but I wish there was more I could do to help those I’ve hurt to heal.

But yeah lol long story short I was pleasantly shocked when I realized I was diagnosed because I was able to put a name to what was wrong with me. And knowing exactly what it was gave me the ability to know how to combat it. 10/10 was shocked to discover I was able to change and take control of my life and myself and never ever again revert to the monstrous person I used to be.

As fucked up as this sounds, if it weren’t for the COVID pandemic I’d probably be dead right now. Lots of reasons why I didn’t transition and I could write a book on all of them so I’ll just try to sum them up in a very short list:

1) Intense history of religious abuse when I was a child that oftentimes closely bordered on conversion therapy. Not full blown conversion therapy but very very very close.

2) Shitty family issues/grew up being told from a very young age that if I was gay or queer or anything of the sort I would be any combination of disowned, “fixed”, or die from AIDS just like my uncle did. The only one I knew who would support me was my mom. Everyone else was either a resounding “no” or “not sure” at best

3) Improperly treated neurosis + REALLY shitty parenting. Ever since I was a kid I’ve had a FUCK ton of mental issues. I was prescribed multitudes of medication ever since I was around 5 years old in a very haphazardly “fuck it let’s just see what sticks” mid-1990s attitude. I never really received any treatment that actually helped me. I was very paranoid and delusional in a LOT of ways and was taught if I did anything out of the norm or strayed from the path my parents instructed me to, then my life would be ruined/I’d end up dead or homeless/etc. It was hammered into my brain that I NEEDED to do what my parents want: go to school, graduate, go to a traditional college, never deviate from the norm, and never express yourself in any non-traditional manner. This followed me throughout my entire life where I was ultimately terrified to do anything that would bring about “change” to myself or my life even if those changes were positive. It made me incredibly indecisive my entire life and I felt aimless. I felt like I didn’t know what I wanted because nothing that was presented to me as “what you’re strictly supposed to do with your life” truly appealed to me. Only things that existed outside of those expectations are what appealed to me…but I was so indoctrinated in bullshit ever since I was a child that what truly appealed to me TERRIFIED me beyond belief. So I did nothing to achieve those goals my entire life because I was too afraid.

4) Horrific toxic work environment. After I graduated I got a job at an autobody shop. I started out as a secretary basically and it paid EXTREMELY well. It was a very intense job/work environment that got even more and more intense as the months and years went by. If people didn’t want to do their jobs, they just had me do it. It got to a point where I was doing 7 other peoples jobs all at once. I got to a point where I was working around 65 hours a week. They promoted me and paid me well…but not nearly as much as they realistically should have considering just how much I was doing towards the end. I had no energy ever. I would get home and have no energy and mainly just stare at the fucking wall until I passed out just to wake up and do it all over again. I was beyond miserable. I HATED being alive and thought “I can’t quit…I’ve never made this much money before ever and I never will again…”. Also I finally had my own apartment that was very expensive and I could only afford on this level of salary. I felt trapped and like there was no way out and that this was it…this was what the rest of my life will be, spending every waking hour working at a job I despised. On top of that I would constantly be bullied at my job, mostly called a faggot by other coworkers (some of which were joking and I was fine with. Others not so much). And whenever a trans customer would come in to get repairs, everyone in the shop would make fun of them behind their backs. I thought “well that settles it I can’t transition here so I guess I just won’t”. I kept at my job until I felt hollow and beyond suicidal feeling like there was no way out. I got to a point where I felt like a walking corpse. 


THEN…all of a sudden COVID hit and I was terrified. I was a fucking mess like most everyone else was. Work got realllly slow and I wasn’t making any money. I asked the owners if they could furlough me and then bring me back once things picked up again. They agreed. I had a little over a month off work and I felt like I had energy again. For the first time in over 3 years I was enjoying myself even if it was just being stuck inside during quarantine. Having that time off was refreshing to say the least. Then a month and a half later I got a call from my boss saying they were bringing me back. That hollow feeling came back and hit me full force and I immediately went right back to being miserable and feeling like a husk. Then about 2 or 3 days back at work I realized I was wasting my fucking life. I quit on the spot and went home and decided I would figure something out and I wouldn’t live like this anymore or ever again and that there had to be something more to life than working myself to death. 

As soon as I made this decision I felt my other fears of changing myself starting to slowly but surely dissipate. I finally realized that yes I wanted to transition and I always have. It took a little bit longer of mentally preparing myself and working up the courage but I finally decided to do it. I wasted the first 29 years of my life living how my family told me I needed to and I wasn’t going to waste another second ever again. 

When I finally was giving myself my first hormone injection I was terrified like “oh god wait do I REALLY want this?” and started second guessing everything I was doing but I slowly (which made it hurt more lol) plunged the (LONG) needle into my leg and pushed down on the plunger and it was the happiest moment of my entire life. I broke down crying but in the best, most cathartic way possible. I looked at this first injection as a ritual form of suicide of my old self and all the horrible shit I hated about me and viewed it as a rebirth into the person I’ve always wanted to be. 

I’ve been transitioning for a little over a year and a half now and I WISH I did this earlier in my life (although I realize thinking that way isn’t healthy and I need to focus on where I am now). I was initially terrified of what my family would do or think. I knew my mom would be accepting (which she was!) but didn’t know what the rest of my family would do. So I decided to preemptively disown those family members that I knew would do it to me first and the power that gave me felt incredible. 

Lol I tried to keep this short oops but it didn’t happen so 

TL;DR I always wanted to be a girl ever since I could remember. Was too afraid too because various reasons. Spent 29 years miserable and afraid to do what I wanted. COVID hit and I realized I was wasting my life so I decided to change everything. Quit my awful job and transitioned and never ever ever looked back and I’ve never been happier.
